 The Toronto Raptors will start Jamal Shead, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles, and Jakob Poeltl against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Scottie Barnes (adductor, groin) will not play in Friday’s game, so the Raptors replaced them with Jamal Shead and Jakob Poeltl. If either of them are available in redraft leagues, they are worth a stream for Friday. Shead would be the priority over Poeltl given the fact that Shead will have the ball more, but most of his value comes from assists. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Poeltl’s status has been upgraded from probable to available. However, he may remain with the second unit after playing 19 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets. Collin Murray-Boyles has started Toronto’s last three games. 
 Immanuel Quickley 
 TOR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) is out for Friday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Added to the injury report Friday afternoon, Quickley will miss the matchup against the Bucks. Jamal Shead is the likely replacement in the starting lineup and is worth streaming in deep leagues. 
 Immanuel Quickley 
 TOR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Bucks. 
 IQ is a late addition to the injury report, which doesn’t bode well for his chances to suit up against Milwaukee. If Quickley ends up sitting out, Jamal Shead could replace him in the starting five. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes (groin) is questionable to play against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Barnes wasn’t initially on the injury report, but he now may miss a game for the first time this season. With Collin Murray-Boyles already in the starting lineup, Jakob Poeltl would likely return to the opening unit if Barnes is out. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett put up 22 points (7-of-17 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three 3-pointers in 128-109 loss to the Nuggets. 
 Barrett led the team in shot attempts in this game and he did a good job scoring the ball. On the season, he’s averaging 20.9 points, 6 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.5 blocks, shooting 48.1% from the field, 59.5% from the free throw line, and 31.8% from three. Outside of the free throw percentage, he’s been great for where he was selected in redraft leagues. There’s even room for him to get better once he starts hitting more of his free throws. 
 Jakob Poeltl 
 TOR 
 Center 
 #19 
 Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 Poeltl was initially listed as questionable with left shoulder bursitis, but has since been cleared for the matchup with the Nuggets Wednesday. With Poeltl returning from a two-game absence, Collin Murray-Boyles will likely head back to the bench. 
 Jakob Poeltl 
 TOR 
 Center 
 #19 
 Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 Poeltl missed Toronto’s last two games: Sunday’s loss to the Lakers and Monday’s win over the Clippers. Collin Murray-Boyles started Monday and will likely keep that role if Poeltl can’t play. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett tallied 26 points (10-of-19 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Clippers. 
 Barrett scored 16 points in the first half of Monday’s game, shooting 7-of-9 from the field. The overall stat line was good, except for one category: free-throw percentage. Barrett is shooting a career-worst 58.8 percent from the charity stripe this season, a number that has done his category league value no favors. That said, Barrett is a career 69.5 percent shooter, so it may not be too surprising that he’s started slowly in that regard. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes (hip) is available for Monday’s game against the Clippers while Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is out. 
 While Barnes is good to go after initially being questionable, Poeltl will miss a second straight game. Trayce Jackson-Davis started Sunday’s loss to the Lakers but wasn’t productive enough to merit streaming in any fantasy league. 
 Jakob Poeltl 
 TOR 
 Center 
 #19 
 Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is now doubtful for Monday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Poeltl did not play in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers, with Trayce Jackson-Davis replacing him in the starting lineup. TJD offered little value in that role, however, so there’s no need to consider streaming him if Poeltl remains out.

 Cooper Flagg with a monster 21 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), ten rebounds, seven assists, three steals, a block and a three in 112-100 win over Jazz on Friday. 
 Flagg scored 15 points in the third quarter which was a big contributor to the Mavericks taking a big lead in second half. His all-around game is valuable for fantasy which can allow for a lot of fantasy builds. He is well on his way to be one of the faces in the league, and for fantasy, his fantasy friendly game will make managers happy for a long time.

 Mario Hezonja tallied 15 points (6-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the 76ers.
 Although he didn’t start on Friday, Hezonja’s role grew in importance because the Cavaliers were without Jarrett Allen (knee). The 6-foot-8 forward, who is bulkier than he was during his first stint in the NBA, led the Cavaliers with 10 rebounds, recording his first double-double of the season. If Allen remains out for Saturday’s game against the Knicks, Hezonja may be worthy of consideration in deep leagues as a streamer.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Peyton Watson (hamstring) accumulated 13 points (6-of-14 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the 76ers.
 Back in the Cavaliers’ lineup after a two-game absence, Watson started and played 28 minutes on Friday. He didn’t record any defensive stats, but the Cavaliers’ forward offered needed contributions on the glass. With Jarrett Allen (knee) out, Watson started at power forward, and his nine rebounds were the most among Cavaliers starters and his most in a game this season. Given the hamstring injury, we’ll see if Watson plays on Saturday against the Knicks.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Evan Mobley accounted for 22 points (8-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the 76ers.
 With Jarrett Allen (knee) out, Mobley thoroughly dominated his matchup with 76ers center Joel Embiid. While “The Process” missed all nine of his field-goal attempts, Mobley shot well over 50 percent from the field and recorded a complete stat line. Through nine games, his fantasy value has aligned with his preseason ADP, a good start for those who invested a third-round pick in Mobley.

 Mitchell didn’t have his most efficient night, shooting 1-for-6 from three and committing four turnovers.  DeAndre Hunter (illness) will not play against the Spurs on Friday, so Leaky Black will get the start. Leaky has been an energy guy who has gained some favor in the eyes of Doug Christie.  Another great game from Kyshawn George who led the team in shot attempts (Check). He was one point away from his career high. (check)He made a lot of winning plays and was a big reason the Wizards stayed in this game, especially in the fourth quarter. He’s been awesome this season and while Anthony Davis was out in this one, he consistently shows up and gets things done. He won’t continue at the level he has been playing at recently, but he’s a very good player. If you have him, it might be worth exploring the market and see if there’s a sell high available.

 Trae Young had 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, ten assists, a steal, three 3-pointers and eight turnovers in a 139-132 loss to the Hawks on Friday. 
 At the end of the game, he hurt his left elbow as he fell to the ground which will be something to monitor. It could be a funny bone, but it’s possible he shows up on the injury report. He finished the game which is a positive sign. In his return to Atlanta, he did his best to lead the Wizards to a win, but to no avail. The league leader in assists continues to be very consistent on that front. It’s not great he had 8 turnovers which left a mark in the turnovers category.

 Tre Johnson scored 23 points (9-of-16 FGs) with one rebound, one assist and five 3-pointers in 27 minutes off the bench in Friday’s loss to the Hawks. 
 Tre Johnson took a lot of the usage vacated by Anthony Davis (ankle) in this game and hit several 3’s. His fantasy game is very empty outside of the scoring and 3’s which limits his fantasy upside, but he is a really good shooter. If AD misses another game, you can consider a stream of Tre Johnson if you’re in need of the points and 3’s. He’s much better in points leagues than category leagues.
